claims.text: BackoffDelay(attempts) = FirstRetryDelay * 2^(attempts-1), capped at MaxRetryDelay; RefundSettings defaults: FirstRetryDelay 1 min, MaxRetryDelay 1 h, GiveUpAfter 24 h.

NextDelay(attempts) returns BackoffDelay(attempts) * (0.5 + Random.Shared.NextDouble() * 0.5): a factor from 0.5 to just under 1, so a wait from half the backoff delay up to the backoff delay, drawn again on every call. Lines 123-132 are marked '// lesson: backend.l3.retry-jitter'.
Random.NextDouble() returns a random floating-point number greater than or equal to 0.0 and less than 1.0; Random.Shared is a shared Random instance.

Without jitter, rows that failed in one round have the same attempt count and get the same wait; when their calls fail quickly (refused connection, e.g. fake-gateway stopped), they come due within moments of each other, one round (BatchSize 10) claims them, and they stay together later.

claims.text: With the defaults, ranges: attempt 1 → 30-60 s, attempt 2 → 1-2 min, attempt 3 → 2-4 min; each range starts where the previous ends, until the 1 h cap, where every wait is 30-60 min.
NotificationSender @ stage-3 (DonHang.Notifications) computes its wait as FirstRetryDelay * 2^(attempts-1) with no random part.

RefundSenderTests @ stage-3 lines 94-107: for attempts 1, 3, 20 (backoff 1, 4, 60 min) it calls NextDelay 1000 times, asserts each is in [backoff/2, backoff] with Assert.InRange, and that there is more than one distinct value.
xUnit Assert.InRange(actual, low, high) passes when actual is within the range low..high; Assert.All runs an assertion on every item of a collection.

The deadline for giving up does not depend on the waits: RecordResult marks the refund failed on the first try again later that comes at least GiveUpAfter (default 24 h) after RequestedAt (now - RequestedAt >= GiveUpAfter).
A retry that comes earlier is still safe because every call for one row sends the same Idempotency-Key refund-<id>.

docker-compose.yml @ stage-3 sets Refunds__FirstRetryDelay "00:00:02" (and Refunds__MaxRetryDelay "00:00:10") for payments, so in the lab the first wait is 1-2 s, a spread under one 2-s round.

Jitter is worth adding when many retries can fail at the same moment and come due together; each wait becomes up to half shorter than the backoff delay, so a refund that keeps failing makes somewhat more attempts before GiveUpAfter.
